maria: FYI - I pulled an nsys + perfetto trace from a prod-like repro and see intermittent ~1.2s cudaMalloc spikes that line up with KV cache refills. timeline looks like: NVTX:kvcache.refill -> cudaMalloc(1.2s) -> packed_attention_fw(400ms) -> memcpyH2D(60ms). attaching a perfetto link: https://perfetto.link/trace/ABc123 (public-ish repro link).

raj: Can you paste the nsys collect command and a short timeline snippet? also which CL/commit did this start showing on?

maria: nsys cmd I used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --output=kvcache_spike run_inference.sh`
small timeline snippet (from nsys GUI):
```
GPU: [0] NVTX: kvcache.refill
  -> cudaMalloc 1.21s
  -> kernel: packed_attention_fw 0.40s
  -> memcpy H2D 0.06s
```
I can upload the full .qdrep if useful. repro is on commit `c8f4a2b` (PR #1428).

hao: quick thought: sounds like allocator falling back to cudaMalloc instead of async pool because of fragmentation in our arena. we saw similar behaviour when concurrent small KV refills interleave with batching worker frees. are we running cudaMallocAsync or our pooled allocator?

maria: runtime is using our internal arena (arena.chunk_size=32MB by default). currently we don't call cudaMallocAsync; we rely on cuMemPool only for the dedicated path. in this repro the kvcache threads spawn ~40 small allocations each concurrently which seems to blow the free-list and triggers slow cudaMalloc on the host.

sylvie: actionable experiments: 1) enable a prealloc persistent arena for the model worker (try 128MB) 2) reduce kvcache refill parallelism (refill_batch=16) so fewer concurrent small allocs 3) tune kernel-selector threshold to prefer the smaller matmul kernel when seq_len < 768 (that avoids the huge temporary that forces a large allocation). do them one-by-one and run the same nsys profile.

perf-bot: quick stat from the trace: "kvcache.refill" threads accounted for 78% of cudaMalloc time in run, model-init 22%. p99 latency delta vs baseline: +0.12s.

raj: the kernel-selector change you mentioned — I think `kernel_selector.cpp` had a default bump in a recent perf PR. can you give the PR/commit? we should verify if selector now prefers the "big" kernel too aggressively.

maria: PR ref is `#1428` commit `c8f4a2b` (same as repro). I ran the prealloc experiment (arena -> 128MB) locally: cudaMalloc spikes dropped ~95% in that run and p99 reduced by ~60ms. I ran: `export REDWOOD_ALLOC_POLICY=persistent_arena && ./run_inference.sh --profile` then re-profiled with nsys. I'll open a reproducible artifact (.qdrep) and attach to the ticket.

hao: good to know. follow-ups: - consider switching kvcache to use our per-thread subarena (avoid cross-thread free-list thrash) - test enabling cudaMallocAsync (if CUDA runtime allows) or use cuMemPool for the worker pool path - add guard in kernel selector: if estimated temp_mem > 64MB, prefer fallback tiled kernel.

sylvie: also add a CI perf-nscheck that runs a short nvtx-instrumented scenario and fails if any cudaMalloc NVTX span > 50ms. that'll catch regressions early.

maria: will open a ticket with steps + attach qdrep + perfetto link + the minimal repro script. tagging @raj @hao @sylvie for review on the remediation plan :thumbsup:

raj: thanks — let's also schedule a quick 15m sync after the ticket with the kernel-selector author to avoid accidental perf toggles. :calendar:

maria: ack, scheduling now.
